title: Passé Composé vs Imparfait - The Golden Rule
description: Learn when to use each past tense: Passé composé for specific events (J'ai mangé - I ate), Imparfait for descriptions/habits (Il faisait beau - It was nice, Je mangeais tous les jours - I used to eat every day)
can_do: Choose the right past tense for every situation
Tell complete stories mixing actions and descriptions
Master the most important past tense distinction in French

vocabulary.gloss: I was eating / I used to eat

concepts.definition: The passé composé tells what happened. The imparfait describes how things were or what used to happen.

examples.en: Yesterday I ate at the restaurant.

examples.fr: D'habitude, je mangeais à la maison.

concepts.definition: Use it for an event that started and finished: the main line of the story.

examples.fr: Hier matin, j'ai pris le bus.
examples.en: Yesterday morning I took the bus.

concepts.term: Imparfait: the scene and the habits
concepts.definition: Use it for descriptions, for states that went on and for things you used to do.

examples.fr: Je prenais le bus tous les matins.
examples.en: I used to take the bus every morning.

concepts.definition: Set the scene in the imparfait, then say what happened in the passé composé.

examples.fr: Il faisait beau quand je suis arrivé.
examples.en: It was nice out when I arrived.

examples.fr: Je prenais un café quand tu es arrivé.
examples.en: I was having a coffee when you arrived.

concepts.term: Words that point to each tense
concepts.definition: {hier} and {soudain} usually go with the passé composé. {tous les jours} and {d'habitude} go with the imparfait.

examples.fr: Hier, je suis allé au café.
examples.en: Yesterday I went to the café.

examples.fr: Je parlais français tous les jours.

examples.en: We usually went to the café.

concepts.definition: The imparfait says what was going on. The passé composé says what cut in.

examples.fr: Je parlais avec Marie quand tu as appelé.
examples.en: I was talking with Marie when you called.

examples.fr: Pendant que je mangeais, tu as appelé.
examples.en: While I was eating, you called.

concepts.definition: Age and a state that lasted take the imparfait. A feeling at one moment can take the passé composé.

items.text: Il ___ beau quand je suis arrivé
items.gloss: It was nice when I arrived

mistakes.feedback: Weather description is background! Use imparfait: il faisait beau.
That's present! Use imparfait for description: il faisait.

items.gloss: Yesterday, I went to the café

mistakes.feedback: Hier = specific time! Use passé composé: je suis allé (I went).
That's present! Use passé composé for yesterday: je suis allé.

items.gloss: I used to speak French every day

mistakes.feedback: Tous les jours = habit! Use imparfait: je parlais (I used to speak).
That's present! Use imparfait for past habit: je parlais.

items.text: Je ___ avec Marie quand tu as appelé
items.gloss: I was talking with Marie when you called

mistakes.feedback: Ongoing action interrupted! Use imparfait: je parlais (I was talking).
That's present! Use imparfait for ongoing past: je parlais.
Soudain = sudden event! Use passé composé: j'ai vu (I saw).
That's present! Use passé composé for past event: j'ai vu.

items.text: Quand j'étais jeune, je ___ avec mon chien
items.gloss: When I was young, I used to play with my dog

mistakes.feedback: Repeated past action (habit)! Use imparfait: je jouais (I used to play).
That's present! Use imparfait for past habit: je jouais.
Both work! But '{étais}' is more natural for ongoing state that day.
That's present! Use imparfait: j'étais content (I was happy).
Description of scene! Use imparfait: il y avait (there were).
That's present! Use imparfait for description: il y avait.
Specific time (at 8h) = specific event! Use passé composé: j'ai mangé.
That's present! Use passé composé for past event: j'ai mangé.

items.text: Pendant que je ___, tu as appelé
items.gloss: While I was eating, you called

mistakes.feedback: Ongoing action (while)! Use imparfait: je mangeais (I was eating).
That's present! Use imparfait for ongoing past: je mangeais.

items.gloss: Usually, we used to go to the café

mistakes.feedback: D'habitude = habit! Use imparfait: on allait (we used to go).
That's present! Use imparfait for past habit: on allait.

items.hint: Choose correct tense for '{tomber}' (tomber malade = get sick)

mistakes.feedback: Getting sick is an event! Use passé composé: je suis tombé malade.
That's present! Use passé composé for past event: je suis tombé.

items.gloss: They used to live in a big apartment

mistakes.feedback: Ongoing past state! Use imparfait: ils habitaient (they used to live).
That's present! Use imparfait for past state: ils habitaient.

items.text: Je ___ le bus tous les matins
items.gloss: I used to take the bus every morning

mistakes.feedback: Tous les matins = habit! Use imparfait: je prenais (I used to take).
That's present! Use imparfait for past habit: je prenais.

items.gloss: Yesterday morning, I took the bus

mistakes.feedback: Hier matin = specific time! Use passé composé: j'ai pris (I took).
That's present! Use passé composé for yesterday: j'ai pris.
Toujours = repeated state! Use imparfait: elle était toujours en retard.
That's present! Use imparfait for past habit: elle était.
À ce moment-là = specific moment! Use passé composé: j'ai compris.
That's present! Use passé composé for past event: j'ai compris.

items.text: Je ___ un café quand tu es arrivé
items.gloss: I was having a coffee when you arrived

mistakes.feedback: Ongoing action (was having)! Use imparfait: je prenais.
That's present! Use imparfait for ongoing past: je prenais.
